title: Normalized restriction transitions and their arbitrary pullback descent
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $k:X\to F$ a map of algebraic spaces with their small etale sites [def-trf-algebraic-space], and $M$ a line module on $F$. Let $(F_i\to F)$ be scheme etale charts, and $(X_i\to X)$ a jointly surjective family of scheme etale charts [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family], indexed in any universe. Suppose maps $a_i:X_i\to F_i$ satisfy equality of their composites to $F$. Write $M_i$ for the Zariski restrictions [def-trf-space-module-scheme-restriction]. Then there exist ordinary invertibility proofs for the $M_i$, normalized ordinary/etale identifications for them, represented double overlaps of the $F_i$, and transition isomorphisms induced by those identifications. There also exist represented double overlaps of the $X_i$, their maps to the original overlaps with both projection equations, and transitions of the literal modules $a_i^*M_i$ equal to the pulled original transitions. They satisfy the diagonal identity and triple-overlap cocycle on every scheme test. There exist a line module $N$ on $X$ and identifications with the literal $a_i^*M_i$ inducing precisely those transitions; they satisfy unique realization preserving every identification. For etale $k$, $N$ has the canonical etale comparison with restriction of $M$, with the prescribed composite-section formula. Normalization, transition transport, uniqueness and the comparison mean exactly the section equations of [def-trf-ample-test-normalized-section-equations], using ordinary identifications [def-sfb-ordinary-etale-identification] and tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. No ampleness hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Apply the scheme ordinary/etale line comparison to each restriction of M. Its tensor-unit normalization, on every Zariski open, yields the original identifications and ordinary invertibility.

Represent both families of double overlaps by the representable diagonals. On original overlaps full faithfulness transports the identity of the same restriction of M to alpha. The given commuting triangles induce the maps of new overlaps to old ones.

Set beta equal to the specified pulled transition. Tensor-section restriction identity and composition laws make its identifications natural. The unit-normalized tensor composition maps are associative, as checked on pure tensors, so they transport the diagonal and cocycle equalities of alpha to beta.

Use effective invertible descent on X to obtain N and identifications inducing beta. Full faithfulness glues the local comparison maps for any other realization, and their local inverses; injectivity proves inverse identities and uniqueness. For arbitrary index universe choose a small covering subfamily by points of one scheme atlas and recover the rest by full faithfulness.

For etale k the restriction of M to X has the same local tensor-pullback identifications, with the tensor-composition section formula. The preceding unique-realization argument glues the prescribed unique isomorphism.
